children: T. S. Eliot picked up on this idea about 5 years after
Portrait
in his best-known essay, “Tradition and the Individual Talent.” In it he states that “the emotion of art is impersonal” and that:

Poetry is not a turning loose of emotion, but an escape from emotion; it is not the expression of personality, but an escape from personality. But, of course, only those who have personality and emotions know what it means to want to escape from these things.
Critical opinion is mixed as to what extent Joyce and Eliot obeyed these precepts in their own work.

annotatable.title: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (Chap. 5)

children: Dedalus' use of the word “forge” here could indicate two things.
1) He could simply be saying that he will create, by use of his own artistic powers, this “conscience of his race.”

2) However, the word “forge” could also be alluding to the act of forgery or false construction. This could imply that Dedalus still feels, in spite of his transcendent experience earlier on with the composition of the villanelle, that this still could be a false vocation, and that at most he can compose – if not anything of meaning – something meaningless yet intricately produced to give the illusion of meaning.

range.content: APRIL 27. Old father, old artificer, stand me now and ever in good stead

6320531.twitter_share_message: “Stephen’s aim is to be an artist for the rest of his life. “The uncreated conscience of my race”…” —@Genius

annotatable.link_title: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (Chap. 5) by James Joyce
annotatable.title: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (Chap. 5)

children: Stephen’s aim is to be an artist for the rest of his life. “The uncreated conscience of my race” implies that he strives to be an artist who uses his individual voice to create a voice and conscience for the community where he was born and raised. The final entry,  where it states “old father” and “old artifices” reinforces Stephen’s dual mission. “Old father” which can be read as either Simon or Ireland itself in order to acknowledge his debt to his past. “Old artificer” references Daedalus, the master craftsman from ancient Greek mythology, this emphasizes his role as an artist. It is through his art that Stephen will use his individuality to create a voice for his community.

7673149.twitter_share_message: “The only response that will allow the mother to take her child back is to state that the alligat…” —@Genius

annotatable.link_title: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (Chap. 5) by James Joyce
annotatable.title: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (Chap. 5)

children: The only response that will allow the mother to take her child back is to state that the alligator will eat the child. If she says the alligator won’t eat the child, then if it does eat the child it makes her statement false, which allows the alligator to keep the child as per its terms. If she says the alligator will eat the child, it has to give the child back, because to not do so (and, presumably, eat the child) would disagree with the alligator’s promise to give the child back if she guessed correctly.
